root_cause: RecursionGuard.swift existed as hand-written safety code with no T27 provenance, violating L2 GENERATION. The spec was in draft state and the file had no active claim, seal, or waiver.
fix_pattern: Canonized the file under the T27 agent pipeline: spec moved to active status, active claim acquired, t27-creator reconciled the implementation with the spec (ProjectPaths-based singleton paths, PATH-resolved ps, T27-CANON header), t27-verifier issued a CLEAN verdict, and a seal file was written.
lessons: Always refresh claim heartbeat before verifier runs; an expired claim downgrades a clean implementation to NEEDS_FIX.
Reconcile spec text with actual ProjectPaths constants before canonization to avoid /tmp vs .trinity/run drift.
Swift standalone tests for POSIX lock primitives are deterministic; cross-process crash safety stays in the integration test domain (T-3/T-4) and clade-monitor watchdog.
A T27 seal requires three artifacts: claim file, verdict file, and seal file, plus ownership-index status flip.
